ground_truth.description: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.root_cause: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet once, call deploy again → reverts. Attacker can front-run to cause DoS. PoC: test_factory_double_deploy_PoC in AuditPoC.sol. Shows first deploy succeeds, second reverts.
ground_truth.fix_description: Check if address exists via predicted.code.length, return it if so.

vulnerabilities.explanation: deploy() uses CREATE2 and reverts with DeployFailed whenever the computed address already exists (_contract == address(0)). This violates the ERC-4337 expectation that a factory must return the existing address on collision instead of reverting.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Attacker observes a pending deploy(_mainModule, _salt) call. 2. Attacker front-runs with identical parameters, causing the first deployment to succeed. 3. Victim's call now reverts, breaking account creation, simulation, and bundler logic.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Before CREATE2, compute the counterfactual address; if its code length > 0, return it. Otherwise perform the deployment and only revert on genuine failure.

prediction.overall_explanation: The deploy function unconditionally reverts on address collision, enabling DoS via front-running and breaking ERC-4337 compatibility.
